title: Logging sidecar for cleaner
description: Add a busybox sidecar that streams cleaner.log from a shared volume to stdout, persist the updated Deployment manifest and inspect the logs.

environmentConstraints: Work only on the instance ckad7326.
No real cluster, container or SSH connection is used in this simulator.
Keep /opt/course/16/cleaner.yaml unchanged and save the updated manifest at /opt/course/16/cleaner-new.yaml.

commands.purpose: Connect to the practice instance.
commands.expectedStdout: Last login: Tue Nov 24 09:00:00 2026 from 10.0.0.1

commands.exact: kubectl -n mercury get deploy cleaner -o yaml
commands.purpose: Inspect the current Deployment, its volume and mount path.
commands.expectedStdout:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cleaner
  namespace: mercury
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cleaner
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cleaner
    spec:
      volumes:
      - name: log-volume
        emptyDir: {}
      containers:
      - name: cleaner-con
        image: busybox:1.31.0
        command:
        - sh
        - -c
        - while true; do echo "cleaner run $(date)" >> /var/log/cleaner/cleaner.log; sleep 2; done
        volumeMounts:
        - name: log-volume
          mountPath: /var/log/cleaner

successCriteria: Deployment cleaner in namespace mercury has a second container named logger-con using image busybox:1.31.0.
logger-con mounts the same log-volume at /var/log/cleaner and runs a tail -f on cleaner.log.
The updated manifest exists at /opt/course/16/cleaner-new.yaml and the original cleaner.yaml is unchanged.
Sidecar logs show ERROR entries about missing data incidents.
rationale: Containers in one Pod share volumes but not filesystems, so a sidecar can read the same emptyDir volume and forward an application log file to stdout for centralized collection.
referenceNotes: A sidecar is an additional container in the same Pod, not a separate Deployment.
Both containers must reference the volume with the same volume name and compatible mount paths.
kubectl logs <pod> -c <container> selects the container whose logs you want to inspect.
Strategic merge patch adds a container when its name is not present in the containers list.

successCriteria: Deployment test-init-container has an InitContainer named init-con using image busybox:1.31.0.

commands.purpose: Verify in-cluster connectivity through the corrected Service DNS name.
commands.expectedStdout: {"status":"ok","service":"manager-api"}

verificationCommands: kubectl -n mars get svc manager-api-svc -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'
kubectl -n mars run tmp-curl --image=nginx:alpine --restart=Never --rm -it -- curl -s manager-api-svc.mars:4444

successCriteria: Service manager-api-svc in namespace mars has selector app=manager-api-deploy matching the Deployment Pod labels.
The Service keeps type ClusterIP and port 4444.
curl from a temporary Pod to manager-api-svc.mars:4444 succeeds.
rationale: A Service routes only to Pods whose labels match its selector; a mismatch creates no Endpoints and therefore no working cluster-internal DNS traffic.
referenceNotes: Check endpoints with kubectl get endpoints <service> to see whether a selector matches Pods.
Service DNS names resolve as <service>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local; the short <service>.<namespace> form also works inside the cluster.
targetPort is the port on the Pod, port is the port exposed by the Service.
Label keys and values in selectors are case-sensitive.

successCriteria: Service jupiter-crew-svc in namespace jupiter has type NodePort with nodePort 30100.
The Service still targets the jupiter-crew-deploy Pods on port 80.
curl to 30100 succeeds against 10.0.0.11, 10.0.0.12 and 10.0.0.13.
The candidate reports that the Pod runs on ckad-node-02 (10.0.0.12).
rationale: A NodePort Service allocates the same static port on every node and kube-proxy forwards it to matching endpoints, so the Service is reachable via any node IP even when the Pod runs elsewhere.
referenceNotes: NodePort range is 30000-32767 by default and must be unique cluster-wide.
Setting type to NodePort keeps the ClusterIP; both access paths remain available.
A request to a node that does not host the Pod is forwarded to a node that does.
Use kubectl get pods -o wide to see the NODE column for Pod placement.

title: Egress NetworkPolicy for frontend
description: Restrict frontend egress to the api Deployment while keeping DNS resolution available, then verify allowed and denied traffic.

environmentConstraints: Work only on the instance ckad7326.
No real cluster, container or SSH connection is used in this simulator.
The policy name must be np1 in namespace venus and DNS on UDP/TCP 53 must remain allowed.

commands.purpose: Connect to the practice instance.
commands.expectedStdout: Last login: Tue Nov 24 09:00:00 2026 from 10.0.0.1

commands.purpose: Inspect Deployments, Services and their label selectors.
commands.expectedStdout:
NAME                          READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE   AGE
 deployment.apps/api          1/1     1            1           9d
 deployment.apps/frontend     1/1     1            1           9d

NAME            TYPE        CLUSTER-IP      EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)    AGE
service/api     ClusterIP   10.96.31.14     <none>        2222/TCP   9d
service/frontend   ClusterIP   10.96.88.7   <none>        80/TCP     9d

commands.exact:
kubectl -n venus apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: np1
  namespace: venus
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: frontend
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: api
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 2222
  - ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
EOF
commands.purpose: Create an egress policy for frontend that allows only api:2222 and DNS.
commands.expectedStdout: networkpolicy.networking.k8s.io/np1 created

commands.exact: kubectl -n venus exec deploy/frontend -- wget -qO- https://www.google.com --timeout=3
commands.purpose: Confirm that general internet egress is denied.
commands.expectedStdout:
wget: download timed out
command terminated with exit code 1

commands.exact: kubectl -n venus exec deploy/frontend -- wget -qO- http://api:2222 --timeout=3
commands.purpose: Confirm that egress to the api Service is still allowed.
commands.expectedStdout: api OK

verificationCommands: kubectl -n venus get netpol np1 -o yaml
kubectl -n venus exec deploy/frontend -- wget -qO- https://www.google.com --timeout=3
kubectl -n venus exec deploy/frontend -- wget -qO- http://api:2222 --timeout=3

successCriteria: NetworkPolicy np1 exists in namespace venus and selects Pods with label app=frontend.
policyTypes contains Egress and the only non-DNS egress rule targets app=api on TCP 2222.
An egress rule allows UDP 53 and TCP 53 for DNS resolution.
wget to www.google.com from frontend fails while wget to api:2222 succeeds.
rationale: NetworkPolicies are additive and namespace-scoped; once Egress is selected for a Pod, all outbound traffic not explicitly allowed by an egress rule is denied, so DNS must be allowed separately.
referenceNotes: An empty egress rule with ports but no to: allows those ports to any destination, which is the usual DNS exception.
podSelector inside an egress to: selects Pods in the same namespace as the NetworkPolicy.
NetworkPolicy requires a CNI plugin that enforces policies.
Use kubectl exec <pod> -- <command> to run connectivity tests inside a running container.

title: Neptune Deployment with ServiceAccount

environmentConstraints: Work only on the instance ckad7326.

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment

successCriteria: All Pods with type=worker or type=runner in namespace sun have label protected=true.
All four Pods with protected=true have annotation protected with value 'do not delete this pod'.

rationale: kubectl label and kubectl annotate accept label selectors, allowing bulk metadata updates; a selector on the newly added label lets the annotation step target exactly the intended Pods.
referenceNotes: Labels are key-value metadata used by selectors; annotations store non-identifying information.
Use -l <key>=<value> to select resources for bulk label or annotate commands.
Add --overwrite when changing the value of an existing label or annotation.
Verify with kubectl get pods --show-labels or jsonpath on metadata.annotations.
